title: Translate a delivered explainer (domain/language reviewer)
context: The shared toolkit separates content strings from data so internationalisation is a cheap downstream task. Once a delivered explainer is available in English, a language and domain reviewer can produce a translation that reaches non-English-speaking communities. The translation must not alter the underlying data derivation, must maintain the plain-language standard in the target language, and must carry the same 'not advice / non-partisan' framing.
objective: Translate one specific previously-delivered explainer into a target language, reviewed by a domain-knowledgeable native-speaker reviewer, maintaining plain-language quality and the 'not advice' framing.
acceptanceCriteria: One specific previously-delivered explainer is translated into a target language, using the content/data separation built into the shared toolkit (toolkit-002).
Translation reviewed by a domain-knowledgeable native speaker for accuracy, appropriate terminology, and plain-language quality in the target language.
Content/data separation maintained: only UI strings and explainer copy are translated; underlying data derivation and source snapshots are not altered.
Output licensed CC-BY-4.0; language/domain reviewer sign-off committed.
Accessibility pass (WCAG 2.2 AA, reading grade <= 8 in the target language) signed off.
resources: PLAN.md — Solution approach (content/data separation for i18n)
toolkit-002 (prerequisite — shared toolkit must exist and implement content/data separation)
output: A translated version of one delivered explainer (committed document in the target language + accessibility sign-off + language/domain reviewer sign-off).
